research_text:
# Research brief: `MessageDigest` and the SM3 finding

## 1. Governed API and meaning of the finding

`java.security.MessageDigest` provides implementations of message-digest algorithms. An application requests an implementation by passing an algorithm name to a `getInstance` factory method, optionally specifying a provider. The finding’s “found SM3” describes the algorithm value associated with an acquisition event—not the digest input or output. The supplied finding does not identify a resolved call, runtime provider, digest purpose, or execution trace. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/java/security/MessageDigest.html))

Oracle’s API documentation is at https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/java/security/MessageDigest.html.

**The reported six-name expectation is not the exact allow-list in the cited CrySL file.** The file lists only `SHA-256`, `SHA-384`, and `SHA-512`. The supplied detector message additionally lists the unhyphenated names `SHA256`, `SHA384`, and `SHA512`; the file alone does not explain that difference. Oracle says algorithm names are case-insensitive and advises standard names rather than provider-dependent aliases. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl))

SM3 is a distinct 256-bit hash algorithm. Its exclusion from this rule is a policy mismatch; the CrySL file does not explain the policy choice or establish the purpose of a particular digest. ([rfc-editor.org](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8998.html))

## 2. Exact rule in the cited source

The published file is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl.

The relevant matching and condition clauses are, verbatim: ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl))

```text
SPEC java.security.MessageDigest

g1: getInstance(algorithm);
g2: getInstance(algorithm, _);
Get := g1 | g2;

algorithm in {"SHA-256", "SHA-384", "SHA-512"};
```

- **Methods and type:** The file declares `java.security.MessageDigest` as its `SPEC` and names `getInstance` for the `Get` event. These are static factory methods, not calls on an existing digest receiver.
- **Parameters:** It specifies either one argument, `algorithm`, or two arguments, `algorithm, _`. It declares `algorithm` as `java.lang.String`; the second argument is written as `_`, without a separate named-variable constraint in this clause. Oracle documents both provider-name and `Provider`-object two-argument overloads. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl))
- **Condition:** The declared algorithm value must be a member of the three-string set quoted above.
- **Same-name methods:** The file does **not** declare a general name-only match for an unrelated type: it specifies `java.security.MessageDigest` and the argument patterns above. A method merely sharing the name `getInstance` is therefore not established as a match by this rule. The file itself does not document a particular detector’s resolution of inherited methods, ambiguous calls, or unresolved types.

The file also specifies `update` and `digest` events, an event order, and array-length constraints. In its exact order expression, the `Update+` branch is followed by `Digest`, which includes all three declared digest events—including `digest(input)`. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl))

## 3. Documented usage and remediation limits

Oracle documents an initialized digest that accepts data through `update`, then completes computation with `digest`; completion resets it. `digest(byte[])` performs a final update followed by completion, so a separate preceding `update` is not required for that API call. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/java/security/MessageDigest.html))

Oracle’s JCA guide illustrates SHA-256 and recommends standard algorithm names. **Neither the `MessageDigest` API documentation nor this CrySL file gives a universal SM3-to-SHA remediation.** Meeting the cited CrySL algorithm predicate would require one of its three named values, but that is distinct from establishing that changing a particular use is compatible or appropriate. The guide is at https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/22/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/13/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html))

For a requirement to authenticate data, Oracle distinguishes the keyed `Mac` API from an unkeyed message digest. An equality comparison alone does not establish that authentication is the purpose of a digest use. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/22/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html))

## 4. Compatibility and migration

- **Persisted and wire formats:** SM3 and SHA-256 are different algorithms, even though both produce 256-bit outputs. Equal output length does not make their values interchangeable. The `MessageDigest` documentation does not define a migration for stored identifiers, caches, external expected values, or protocol formats; those contracts must be established separately. An unchanged external contract cannot be assumed to accept a different digest. ([rfc-editor.org](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8998.html))
- **Platform support:** Oracle’s Java 8 API lists SHA-256 among required algorithms, while Java 26 lists SHA-256 and SHA-384. The lists differ by release; the documentation directs readers to the implementation’s release documentation for additional algorithms. A named provider must itself support the requested algorithm, or acquisition can fail. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/security/MessageDigest.html))
- **Migration path:** The cited API sources provide no general versioning, conversion, or dual-read migration procedure for changing digest algorithms. Compatibility evidence depends on whether the digest is a transient discriminator, cache key, persisted identifier, security digest, or part of an external contract.

## 5. Source limitations and unresolved questions

The CrySL URL points to the mutable `master` branch. The detector’s bundled rule revision was not supplied, and the provided SHA-256 identifier was not independently verified against a bundled file. The source therefore cannot establish why this report lists six names rather than the file’s three, how the detector resolved the reported call, or whether its value was known at runtime. No conclusion about a particular repository’s behavior or deployed system follows from the supplied finding.
